slides.title: Pluralistic Human-Robot Interaction: Designing for Robot Interaction with Diverse Communities
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR INCLUSIVE SOCIAL ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to address social complexity and human diversity in robot deployment, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to treat human diversity as a foundational social robot design concern.
card.key_idea: A framework integrating seven principles: pluralism, civic dialogue, perspective-taking, empathy, intercultural competence, cultural humility, and moral imagination to create inclusive, adaptive, and ethically grounded interactions.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines proposed evaluation metrics (e.g., inclusion, dialogue quality) rather than reporting experimental results.
card.limitation: Risks include reinforcing stereotypes, excluding non-normative users, and privileging dominant cultural assumptions if pluralism is not integrated.

slides.title: Galaxy General Unveils Self-Learning Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: SELF-LEARNING HUMANOID ROBOT
slides.highlight: The introduction of a self-learning humanoid robot demonstrates an inflection point in embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: China Telecom leads embodied AI startup Mifeng funding
slides.tldr: MIFENG SECURES FUNDING
slides.highlight: Mifeng, an embodied AI startup, has received funding led by China Telecom. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: Physics of Agents: Statistical Mechanics Predicts Collective Behavior of AI Agents
slides.tldr: STATISTICAL MECHANICS PREDICTS AI AGENT COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research uses a statistical-mechanics formalism to predict collective dynamics, such as polarization and consensus, in communities of language-model agents. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Statistical mechanics predicts collective AI agent behavior, showing interactions drive conviction and truth-seeking on objective tasks.
card.key_idea: An Ising-model-based formalism where agents update opinions to minimize social pressure, combining intrinsic biases with signed-network interactions (concordant/discordant ties) via a stochastic update rule.
card.evaluation: Simulated >10,000 communities across 4 LLMs, objective math and subjective political questions, and various network graphs; outperformed standard baselines in trajectory prediction.
card.limitation: Subjective questions showed systematic ideological drift toward the right, suggesting interaction may amplify underlying language model biases.

slides.title: Insurance as AI Risk Infrastructure: A Generative-Agent Simulation of AI Adoption
slides.tldr: INSURANCE-BASED AI ADOPTION SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This work uses an LLM-driven agent-based social simulation to analyze how insurance frameworks can mitigate financial risks and accelerate AI adoption, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Insurance accelerates AI adoption by hedging financial risks, reducing bankruptcies and increasing aggregate capital in simulations.
card.key_idea: An LLM-driven agent-based social simulation (LABSS) where heterogeneous firms make AI adoption and insurance decisions based on bounded attention and risk assessment.
card.evaluation: Validated via mechanism diagnostics and path-level tests across three matched replications; results showed AI adoption rose from 74.97% to 84.38% with insurance.
card.limitation: The study relies on a simulated environment with stylized vendors and insurers rather than real-world market data.

slides.title: Closing the Affective Loop: Multimodal Speaker-Listener Emotion-Dynamics-Aware Empathetic Social Robots
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL EMOTION-DYNAMICS-AWARE DIALOGUE SYSTEM
slides.highlight: This work introduces AffectLoop, a system that tracks speaker verbal and facial affective dynamics alongside the listener's state to improve embodied empathetic interaction, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: AffectLoop enables social robots to generate empathetic responses by tracking both speaker and listener affective dynamics.
card.key_idea: An LLM-based system conditioning responses on multimodal speaker trajectories (verbal VAD and facial affect) and the robot's own verbal/behavioral affective states to close the affective loop.
card.evaluation: Pilot within-subject study (5 participants) using Likert scales and log analysis. Results show higher user satisfaction, affective alignment, and distress recovery than a text-only baseline.
card.limitation: Preliminary results based on a very small sample size (five participants) in a pilot study.

slides.title: Bayesian Partner Modelling enables Adaptive Replanning for LLM Coordination
slides.tldr: BAYESIAN PARTNER TRACKING FOR ADAPTIVE LLM REPLANNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces BayesBeliefAgent, which uses a Bayesian tracking module to infer partner skills and trigger adaptive replanning in Overcooked environments. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that infer partner intent and adapt at test time for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: BayesBeliefAgent uses Bayesian partner modeling to trigger selective replanning only when teammate actions contradict beliefs.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical LLM planner paired with a Bayesian tracking module that interrupts current skills when observed partner actions have low likelihood under the current skill estimate.
card.evaluation: Tested in Overcooked/Burrito environments against LLM and RL baselines using reward, belief-action gap, and replanning efficiency metrics. Results show significantly fewer replans.
card.limitation: The underlying LLM-based high-level skill planner remains a major performance bottleneck compared to RL-based coordination agents.

slides.title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training
slides.tldr: LEARNING PERSONALIZED THERAPIST-PATIENT INTERACTIONS FOR REHABILITATION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Learning-from-Demonstration framework to capture personalized physical therapist-patient interactions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction in embodied learning contexts.

card.one_liner: A framework to learn and generalize personalized therapist-patient physical interactions for robot-mediated upper limb rehabilitation.
card.key_idea: Uses Task-Parameterised Gaussian Mixture Models (TPGMM) to map patient joint kinematics to therapist-applied torques, generalizing from few demonstrations to unseen task variations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 14 mock therapist-patient pairs across three tasks. TPGMM was compared against a Look-Up Table (LUT) using reconstruction error and coverage.
card.limitation: Reproduced interactions in unseen variations deviated slightly from actual interactions; results were based on mock pairs (physiotherapy students).

slides.title: Hippocratic AI rolls out platform to coordinate teams of conversational voice AI agents
slides.tldr: COORDINATION OF CONVERSATIONAL VOICE AI AGENT TEAMS
slides.highlight: The development of a platform to coordinate teams of conversational voice AI agents is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

slides.title: LLMs Can Predict Failure Risk, But Struggle to Predict Which Collaboration Protocol Pays Off: Cost-Aware Protocol Routing Across Reasoning Tasks
slides.tldr: LLMS PREDICT FAILURE RISK BUT STRUGGLE WITH PROTOCOL ROUTING
slides.highlight: This research explores the ability of LLMs to predict failure risk and select optimal collaboration protocols, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and adapting agentic behaviors for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: LLMs can predict their own failure risk but struggle to select the most cost-effective collaboration protocol.
card.key_idea: The authors distinguish between 'failure-risk prediction' (will Baseline fail?) and 'collaboration-value prediction' (which expensive protocol justifies its cost?), testing four protocols across multiple reasoning benchmarks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 4,181 OmniMath problems and four other benchmarks using gpt-oss-120b and Gemma-4-31B-it; metrics include AUROC, AUPRC, solve rate, and token cost.
card.limitation: Post-answer confidence is weak at predicting protocol-specific value; results are based on deterministic runs rather than stochastic variability.

slides.title: HODAgent: Towards On-Demand, Responsive Humanoids for Physical World Human Interaction
slides.tldr: RESPONSIVE HUMANOID SERVICE AGENT
slides.highlight: HODAgent introduces a System-2 embodied agent for humanoid robots that enables responsive task revision and outcome verification during human interaction, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HODAgent is a System-2 embodied agent enabling responsive, on-demand human-humanoid interaction in simulated and physical environments.
card.key_idea: A semi-duplex architecture coordinating an Env-Interactor, Planner, Executor, and hierarchical Memory to handle requests during active robot motion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a User Agent framework in simulation (164 cases) and on a Unitree G1; outperformed ReAct baselines in Joint Success.
card.limitation: Does not establish full-duplex interaction, hard real-time guarantees, broad cross-robot generalization, or task-level sim-to-real transfer.

slides.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge
slides.tldr: MULTILINGUAL CONVERSATIONAL SPEECH MODELING
slides.highlight: This work addresses speaker diarization and recognition in unsegmented multilingual conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and identity recognition.

card.one_liner: Improves multilingual conversational speech diarization and understanding using leading-silence augmentation and synthetic QA supervision.
card.key_idea: Task 1 uses random leading-silence cropping and EMA training on VibeVoice-ASR-7B. Task 2 employs synthetic QA generation with silent-audio filtering and distribution-matched augmentation for Qwen3-Omni.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MLC-SLM Challenge sets; Task 1 reduced tcpMER from 18.30% to 16.73%, and Task 2 increased accuracy from 78.0% to 86.0%.
card.limitation: Ablations do not establish robustness to turn-boundary errors or provide per-language and onset-conditioned performance analysis.

slides.title: Implementation of a Metacognition Framework for Self-Awareness and Self-Regulation in Ensembles of LLMs
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE FRAMEWORK FOR LLM ENSEMBLES
slides.highlight: This work introduces a metacognitive framework using a Metacognitive State Vector to enable self-awareness and self-regulation in LLM ensembles, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction.

card.one_liner: A metacognition framework for LLM ensembles using a state vector to regulate self-awareness and processing.
card.key_idea: A Metacognitive State Vector (MSV) monitors five psychological dimensions to trigger switching between fast System 1 and deliberative System 2 processing with graph-theoretic role assignments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a Proof-of-Concept demo with illustrative qualitative examples (factual, technical, and complex queries) and real-time visualizations.
card.limitation: MSV dimensions are currently self-reported; single-channel validation of state-of-the-art approaches is relegated to future work.

slides.title: Engineering Signals of Human-AI Collaboration in the Agentic Coding Era
slides.tldr: LONGITUDINAL ANALYSIS OF HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION IN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING
slides.highlight: This study analyzes human-AI collaboration signals and development velocity in open-source repositories, providing empirical data on how AI assistants influence human productivity and interaction patterns relevant to MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: AI-assisted development significantly increases software throughput and contributor participation in high-velocity open-source AI infrastructure projects.
card.key_idea: Longitudinal analysis of seven engineering metrics across four eras in vLLM and SGLang repositories to track human-AI collaboration signals and development velocity.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 33,228 merged PRs from vLLM and SGLang using metrics like throughput, cycle time, and comment density. Results show substantial velocity increases.

slides.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models
slides.tldr: TRAINING-FREE INFERENCE-TIME SELF-REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces EvoResearcher, a protocol for cost-bounded self-reflection and self-verification using a frozen LLM backbone. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction for adaptive AI teammates.

card.one_liner: EvoResearcher is a training-free, cost-bounded self-reflection protocol that improves LLM reasoning via an iterative generate-critique-revise loop.
card.key_idea: A frozen LLM uses a prompt-based 'CONFIRMED' sentinel and maximum depth D to early-stop self-reflection, guided by a four-component meta-reward design principle.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BBH, GSM8K, and MATH using deepseek-v4-flash and Qwen2.5-72B; showed accuracy gains on MATH (+14.2pp) and GSM8K (+4.2pp) with 82-88% early-stopping.
card.limitation: Tool-call diversity and multi-agent extensions are design blueprints only and were not evaluated on tool-using benchmarks like GAIA.

slides.title: Collective Counterfactual Planning: Coordination, Consent, and Verification under Representational Constraints
slides.tldr: FORMAL MODEL FOR COLLECTIVE PLANNING UNDER REPRESENTATIONAL CONSTRAINTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a formal model for Collective Counterfactual Planning where agents operate via projections onto agent-specific subspaces, relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent coordination.

card.one_liner: A formal model of collective planning where agent limitations are defined by representational subspace geometry.
card.key_idea: Collective Counterfactual Planning (CCP) uses orthogonal projections to gate conception, consent, and verification, enabling solutions via iterated cross-agent relay that individual plans cannot achieve.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via machine-checked numerical examples (E1, E2) and formal theorems proving the duality of collective reach and representational blindness.
card.limitation: Goals depending on the 'dark subspace' (invisible to all agents) are unverifiable and cannot be validly completed.

slides.title: Beyond LLM-Based Reasoning: Lightweight GNNs for Agent Failure Attribution
slides.tldr: LIGHTWEIGHT GNN FOR AGENT FAILURE ATTRIBUTION
slides.highlight: Introduces AFANet, a graph-based framework for identifying faulty agents and error types in multi-agent trajectories. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: AFANet uses lightweight GNNs to attribute multi-agent system failures, outperforming expensive LLM-based reasoning methods.
card.key_idea: A GNN framework modeling interaction trajectories as conversation graphs using turn-level semantic, statistical, and deviation features with temporal and intra-agent edges.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AEGIS-Bench and Who&When against pre-trained, fine-tuned, and proprietary LLMs using Micro/Macro-F1; results show superior pair-level accuracy and efficiency.
card.limitation: Generalizing agent failure attribution under severe distribution shift remains an inherently challenging problem.

slides.title: Procedural Collapse: A Structural Account of Disengagement in LLM-Assisted Writing
slides.tldr: STRUCTURAL CAUSES OF LLM DISENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This research identifies 'procedural collapse' in AI writing interfaces, suggesting that restructuring interactions and goal elicitation can reduce the burden on users to self-regulate. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and designing AI teammates that support human cognitive work.

card.one_liner: LLM-assisted writing disengagement is a structural interaction failure, not just a lack of user self-regulation.
card.key_idea: Procedural collapse occurs when single-output interfaces replace iterative writing with a high-cost evaluation task, overloading working memory and causing shallow engagement with AI-generated text.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper presents a theoretical framework and design directions rather than an empirical study.
card.limitation: The paper provides a generative framework and predictions but does not provide experimental data to validate them.

slides.title: tinyDSM: A Framework for Skill Modeling and Development for Resource-Constrained Millirobots
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS SKILL ACQUISITION FOR MILLIROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for autonomous skill acquisition and adaptation in resource-constrained robots, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill development and adaptive learning loops.

card.one_liner: tinyDSM enables resource-constrained millirobots to autonomously learn and adapt motion skills using intrinsic motivation.
card.key_idea: A cognitive architecture combining a hierarchical knowledge graph, kinematic reasoners, and intrinsic motivation (novelty, progress, difficulty) to guide reinforcement learning on low-power microcontrollers.
card.evaluation: Tested on a 150g millirobot (RP2040) and simulations; robot learned basic to complex geometric patterns within 15 minutes.
card.limitation: Currently relies on a host device for pose estimation via camera, restricting autonomy to controlled environments.

slides.title: CogChat: Knowledge Graph-Augmented Conversational AI with Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for Cognitive Grounding in Design Generation
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE GRAPH-AUGMENTED CONVERSATIONAL AI
slides.highlight: CogChat uses a heterogeneous knowledge graph and transformer to maintain relational context and personalized intent in conversations, supporting HyECHO's goals for advanced listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: CogChat uses a personal heterogeneous knowledge graph and HGT to ground conversational AI in design.
card.key_idea: It extracts typed entities into a heterogeneous graph, using a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (HGT) for selective context injection and generating intentional and exploratory probing questions.
card.evaluation: Technical benchmarks (ASQA, RewardBench, LoCoMo, LongMemEval) and a within-subjects study with nine professional designers showed improved context retention and lower cognitive load.

slides.title: DuplexGen: Decoupling Content, Timing, and Acoustics for Synthetic Dialogue Speech
slides.tldr: SYNTHETIC DIALOGUE FRAMEWORK FOR NATURAL CONVERSATIONAL TIMING
slides.highlight: DuplexGen enables natural emergence of conversational timing, overlaps, and backchannels, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: DuplexGen synthesizes conversational speech by decoupling scripted content, emergent interaction timing, and high-fidelity acoustic rendering.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates scripts, two full-duplex models perform them via real-time interaction to determine timing, and a TTS system re-renders the result while preserving relative timing.
card.evaluation: Compared against stitching baselines using PriMock57; showed better distributional realism (lower Wasserstein distance/KS statistic) and validated via ASR stress tests on a medical benchmark.
card.limitation: Interaction is only partially emergent via control parameters, lacks mid-utterance interruptions, and prevents speakers from revising content after being interrupted.

slides.title: VTInstructor: Visual Trajectory Prompting for Navigation Instruction Generation in Continuous Environments
slides.tldr: NEW FRAMEWORK FOR NAVIGATION INSTRUCTION GENERATION
slides.highlight: VTInstructor generates navigation instructions from ego-centric RGB video in continuous environments, enhancing human-robot interaction and follower success rates. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: VTInstructor generates navigation instructions from continuous RGB video using explicit visual trajectory prompts.
card.key_idea: Converts implicit trajectory geometry into visual prompts (path ribbons, turn arrows, goal markers) injected into a ViT encoder via a gated modulator and refined using VT-GRPO.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val Unseen using NLG metrics and frozen-follower success rates; outperformed baselines, achieving 63.3% success rate.
